issues.failure_explanation: The text infers dDh(eta)=d_v(msL) on solutions from d_v(dDh eta)=0 holding only on solutions. That step requires the vertical complex restricted to the solution submanifold to be exact at (p,1). For the difference bicomplex the paper proves vertical exactness only on the full prolongation space Z^p x P_n(R^q) (Appendix), and states the restricted-vertical-cohomology fact only for PDEs (Section 2.1/2.2); the needed closedness d_v(dDh eta)=0 holds only on solutions, so Theorem thm:added-2 does not apply. For systems whose solution fibres are not contractible the implication can fail, so the proposed passage from a multisymplectic structure to a Lagrangian msL ('a Lagrangian form for the system') needs a standard local-solvability hypothesis that is never stated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis that the prolonged system is locally solvable with vertically contractible solution fibres (the condition under which the differential-case fact invoked in Section 2.1 holds), or state and prove restricted vertical exactness for the difference bicomplex under that hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised 'systematic method' proceeding from a multisymplectic structure to an equivalent difference Lagrangian structure is unsupported as written. issues.title: Multisymplectic-to-Lagrangian step uses vertical exactness on the solution submanifold, unestablished for the difference bicomplex
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local hypothesis restores the step with no change to any formal result, method, or example; the repair is short and local.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (However, these equations may be weaker than the given system and so admit other solutions.)

the $(p,0)$-form $\msL$ is a Lagrangian form for the
system of P$\Delta$Es.

issues.failure_explanation: The sentence claims the converse direction: any linear system of PDeltaEs with a vertically closed (p-1,2)-form omega satisfying dDh omega=0 has a Lagrangian of the specific first-order degenerate form (lp), i.e. is the Euler--Lagrange system (el) of such a Lagrangian -- the reading required by the 'Therefore' that follows. No argument is given. The paper's own construction yields only a (p,0)-form on the solution submanifold whose Euler--Lagrange equations vanish on solutions, may be weaker than the given system (a caveat the paper itself states for PDEs), and need not be of the form (lp). Multisymplecticity is a single scalar condition D_{n^i}kappa^i=0 on solutions and does not force a (linear) system into the variational form (el), whose zeroth-order part must be a gradient dH/du^alpha; so under its operative reading the claim is false in general, and the linearity hypothesis is left unmotivated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the sentence, or weaken it to what the text supports: a standard vertically closed omega yields (via the vertical homotopy on the fibres) an (lp)-type Lagrangian whose multisymplectic form is omega and whose Euler--Lagrange equations hold on solutions of the given system but may be weaker than it, mirroring the paper's own caveat for PDEs.
issues.overall_effect: Only this remark and the heuristic justification for treating multisymplectic systems as difference Euler--Lagrange equations are affected; Theorem thm:added-1 is conditional on (con) and does not use the converse.
issues.title: Unsupported converse claim: existence of an (lp)-form Lagrangian for linear multisymplectic systems
issues.why_classification: An isolated heuristic remark with no labelled result depending on it; a short local qualification or deletion preserves everything the paper actually uses.

issues.failure_explanation: As stated, the vertical complex is claimed exact at every stage including Omega^{k,0}. That is false: ker(d_v : Omega^{k,0} -> Omega^{k,1}) consists of (k,0)-forms whose coefficients do not depend on [u] (e.g. any nonzero function f(n), or f(n)Delta^{i_1}...Delta^{i_k}), which are d_v-closed but not d_v-exact. The proof only establishes exactness at Omega^{k,l} for l>=1: the homotopy h_v^{k,l} is defined only for l>=1 and the homotopy identity sigma = d_v h_v^{k,l}(sigma) + h_v^{k,l+1}(d_v sigma) is valid for l>=1, as the proof itself notes. The same overstatement appears in the review of the differential bicomplex.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate: for each k the vertical complex is exact at Omega^{k,l} for all l>=1 (equivalently, augment each column on the left by the pure difference k-forms on Z^p).
issues.overall_effect: Only the theorem's wording is wrong. Every application of vertical exactness in the paper (omega=d_v eta with l=2, dDh eta = d_v msL with l=1, v_xi contraction omega = d_v lambda_xi with l=1, the Section 4 Hamiltonian with l=1) uses stages l>=1, which the proof does establish.
issues.title: Vertical exactness overstated: the complex is not exact at Omega^{k,0}
issues.why_classification: A one-line scope correction; the given proof already proves exactly the corrected statement and no downstream claim changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Exactness at Omega^{p,l} is asserted to follow from '(eq:ii)'. That label refers to the differential identity; its difference analogue appears in the main text justified by 'As I^Delta is a projection and the difference variational bicomplex is exact, a difference version of (eq:ii) holds' -- i.e. it is derived from the very exactness theorem under proof, so the citation is circular. The displayed homotopy identity (eq:hohomo), stated for all 1<=k<=p, is what should prove this stage directly, but at k=p (where Omega^{p+1,l}=0) it reads dDh(h^{p,l} sigma)=sigma, which is false: for p=1 and sigma=f(n,[u]) Delta^1 wedge d_v u^alpha_0 in Omega^{1,1}, the displayed formula gives F^{I+1}_alpha(partial_{n^1} contraction sigma)=0 for every I, hence h^{1,1}_h(sigma)=0 and dDh h^{1,1}_h(sigma)=0, not sigma; consistently sigma is not dDh-exact, since I^Delta(sigma) is nonzero while im(dDh) is contained in ker I^Delta by (coch). The correct top-degree identity is dDh o h^{p,l} = id - I^Delta (equivalently the difference (eq:ii) with tau = -h^{p,l} sigma), which the same formula does satisfy; as written, neither the cited premise nor the stated identity validly yields exactness at Omega^{p,l}. The proof of thm:added-4 invokes the same difference version of (eq:ii) twice, so it inherits the gap.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (eq:hohomo) for 0<=k<=p-1 and add the top-degree identity dDh o h^{p,l} = id - I^Delta (with h^{p+1,l}=0), which the same formula satisfies; derive the difference version of (eq:ii) from it, giving ker(I^Delta)=im(dDh) without circularity (or cite the direct proof in [HyMa2004]). The verification is the same summation-by-parts computation as for the other stages.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the appendix does not validly prove exactness of the augmented horizontal complex at Omega^{p,l} (thm:added-3) or of the boundary complex (thm:added-4) -- the paper's central structural results, on which the difference (eq:ii)/(eq:dvLag), the Noether conservation law (eq:Noecl), the Section 4 Hamiltonian existence, and the Section 5 constructions all rely. The statements themselves are correct and standard, and the displayed homotopy formula supports the corrected identity, so the defect lies in the written proofs, not in the results.
issues.title: Top-degree horizontal exactness justified circularly, and the stated homotopy identity (eq:hohomo) fails at k=p
issues.why_classification: No result is lost and the repair is contained -- a corrected displayed identity plus a standard computation within one proof -- but it is a genuine replacement argument in the paper's central exactness theorem (also repairing thm:added-4's reliance on the same identity), which exceeds a short local fix while requiring no new global architecture.
